tools.name: dropyour_publish_site
tools.description: Publish a MULTI-FILE site from a .zip (index.html + css/js/images), base64-encoded. Requires a Pro account token — your tier is anonymous. Same permanent URL; assets served under the drop. Max 25 MB, up to 50 files.

tools.name: dropyour_status
tools.description: Get a drop's status: URL, visibility, expiration, size, approximate view count, and its private name (if set). With an account token, owned drops need no managementToken.

tools.name: dropyour_delete
tools.description: Permanently delete a drop. Immediate and final — the URL is never reassigned. With an account token, owned drops need no managementToken.

tools.name: dropyour_list
tools.description: List your drops. With an account token: all LIVE drops attached to your account (across sessions and channels — manageable without managementToken). Anonymous: only the drops published during this MCP session. Management tokens are never stored server-side.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: dropyour_status, dropyour_read_content · Private data: dropyour_whoami, dropyour_publish, dropyour_publish_site, dropyour_replace, dropyour_update_settings, dropyour_status, dropyour_read_content, dropyour_read_data, dropyour_write_data, dropyour_delete, dropyour_list · Public sink: dropyour_publish, dropyour_publish_site · Destructive: dropyour_publish, dropyour_publish_site, dropyour_replace, dropyour_update_settings, dropyour_status, dropyour_read_content, dropyour_read_data, dropyour_write_data, dropyour_delete.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: dropyour_status, dropyour_read_content · Private data: dropyour_whoami, dropyour_publish, dropyour_publish_site, dropyour_replace, dropyour_update_settings, dropyour_status, dropyour_read_content, dropyour_read_data, dropyour_write_data, dropyour_delete, dropyour_list · Public sink: dropyour_publish, dropyour_publish_site · Destructive: dropyour_publish, dropyour_publish_site, dropyour_replace, dropyour_update_settings, dropyour_status, dropyour_read_content, dropyour_read_data, dropyour_write_data, dropyour_delete

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.

remediation.title: Tool description changed since last scan
remediation.detail: Tool "dropyour_status" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
